body:
Real triage note (PM merge dispatch UMR-20260806-132552-9558), leaving OPEN -- not superseded, not merging today.

Unlike #7/#11/#17 (all confirmed byte-identical-already-upstream by git's own rebase 'patch contents already upstream' detection), this PR is genuinely NOT redundant: its own code comment is explicit that the new `log-entity`/`log-relation`/`check-conflict` coordination-graph commands are 'distinct from register-entity/lookup-entity/list-entities (those are wiring_registry's code-wiring entities, a different table and taxonomy entirely)' -- a different, additive feature (cross-session claim-conflict detection), not a duplicate of what already merged.

Rebasing onto current origin/main produces a real conflict in superboss-register.py (3 hunks, all 'two independently-added CLI subcommand blocks at the same insertion point' shape, same as PR #172's conflict pattern -- resolvable, not a logical clash). Given the size (550 lines across superboss-register.py, dispatch-owner-task.sh, check-conflict-before-pr.sh, backfill_active_claims.py) and that it touches dispatch-owner-task.sh (a live-traffic-critical file), a proper review needs dedicated conflict-resolution + re-test time beyond this dispatch's scope, not a rubber-stamp merge or a default close. Recommending a follow-up task specifically for this PR rather than acting on it further here.

AUDIT: PASS
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-8-feat-add-entity-relation-coordination-gr' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  backfill_active_claims.py   | 161 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 check-conflict-before-pr.sh |  43 ++++++++
 dispatch-owner-task.sh      |  41 ++++++++
 superboss-register.py       | 239 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 484 insertions(+)
Evidence Recorded: This is a well-built, additive coordination-graph feature (new entity/relation SQLite tables plus log-entity/log-relation/check-conflict CLI commands in superboss-register.py, a warning-only conflict check wired into dispatch-owner-task.sh's Step 0 and a new post-registration Step 4.5 self-claim, a standalone check-conflict-before-pr.sh wrapper, and a one-time backfill script) that I verified by live-testing against a scratch SQLite DB rather than trusting the diff's own comments: entity/relation creation, idempotent get-or-create, shallow metadata merge on re-log, bidirectional path-prefix conflict matching, open/closed status exclusion, and transitive depends_on/implemented_by issue-narrowing via the recursive CTE all behaved exactly as documented. All SQL is parameterized (no injection risk), every new integration point is non-blocking and fails open (subshell fallbacks, `|| true`, warning-only exit codes), no .github/workflows/** files are touched, and nothing in the diff matches the tier2 trigger paths (migrations, schema.sql, auth, permission/payment/billing/rls/security, .env) so the tier1 classification is consistent with the actual change. The one real defect I found by reproducing it live: backfill_active_claims.py's _load_yaml_tolerant() only guards its *first* yaml.safe_load() attempt in a try/except; the second parse of the heuristically re-indented text (line ~85) is unguarded, so a very plausible variant of the exact malformed-entry shape it was written to tolerate (continuation lines like `claim:`/`scope_note:` left at their original 4-space indent rather than uniformly shifted with the broken `- session_label:` line) still raises an uncaught yaml.ParserError and crashes the whole script instead of degrading gracefully as the docstring promises. This is confined to a standalone, manually-invoked, read-only-on-source, idempotent one-time migration helper -- it cannot corrupt ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml or the coordination-graph DB, nothing else in the pipeline depends on it succeeding, and it fails loudly (traceback) rather than silently, so it does not block approval of the rest of this additive, low-blast-radius change. Issues found: backfill_active_claims.py: _load_yaml_tolerant()'s second yaml.safe_load() call (after heuristic re-indentation) is not wrapped in try/except, so a malformed ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml entry whose continuation lines (claim:/scope_note:) are not uniformly shifted with the broken column-0 '- session_label:' line still crashes the script with an unhandled ParserError instead of skipping that entry -- verified by reproducing this exact shape against a synthetic file. Recommend wrapping the retry parse in its own try/except that logs a warning and skips/aborts gracefully rather than raising, in a follow-up.
Severity Classified: none
Verdict: pass
Corrective Action Owner: Not required -- no issues found in this review.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Not required -- approved as-is, no follow-up needed.
